samples.source: walks drawn per question; a starting value, to be fitted from the kept_after curve in sample.py's report (the count where questions with a kept walk stops growing) on the dev world

temperature.source: the model's own distribution over the options (no sharpening or flattening); the walks it would make by chance, filtered by execution

preview.source: the planner configuration the adapter will serve, previews on (data fields): measured 89/109 against 87/109 decisions on the dev planner bench (graph/planner/bench/results/bench-20261026T043512.json)

seed.source: fixed so a sampling run reproduces

heldout_percent.source: held-out share of worlds (questions when there is one world) for early stopping; carried from the capability tuning brief (graph-tune branch)

iters.source: an upper bound; the run ends earlier by patience or the time cap (carried from the capability tuning run)

lora_rank.source: small rank (carried from the capability tuning run)

lora_layers.source: mlx-lm's default count of top layers adapted

learning_rate.source: a starting point for a one-token target; the held-out loss curve decides the checkpoint (carried from the capability tuning run)

grad_accumulation.source: batch size 1 with gradient accumulation (carried from the capability tuning run)

steps_per_eval.source: validate every 250 steps (carried from the capability tuning run)

patience_evals.source: evaluations without a held-out improvement before stopping; a starting value, not fitted

max_hours.source: time cap of a training run; a starting value, not fitted

mlx_memory_limit_gb.source: training is memory-capped so other work keeps running (carried from the capability tuning run)

mlx_cache_limit_gb.source: a small MLX cache (carried from the capability tuning run)

min_free_disk_gb.source: a run keeps the best and the latest adapter plus metrics, well under 1 GB
